articles.title: From Democracies to Autocracies: How AI Systems Enable Authoritarianism by Design
articles.summary: arXiv:2606.17286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-enabled authoritarianism is not confined to autocracies. articles.title: Narratives That Limit the Possible: Interrupting Narrative Closure in Computing Practice
articles.summary: arXiv:2606.17360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computing's dominant concepts - innovation, efficiency, resilience, professionalism - often migrate from reflective ideals to instruments that limit behaviour, redirect responsibility, and foreclose critique. We call this drift weaponisation: the discursive repurposing of professional concepts so that they stabilise business-as-usual while making structural alternatives appear unreasonable, illegible, or out of scope. articles.title: Towards Auditing AI Systems in the Wild
articles.summary: arXiv:2606.17367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems are increasingly deployed in real-world settings where their behavior is shaped by dynamic environments, evolving data distributions, and complex interactions with users and infrastructure. Traditional machine learning evaluation focuses on benchmarks and operates within sandboxed environments, providing only a limited view of the true system behavior in the wild. articles.title: Self-Efficacy and Favorability Shape Learning from Tutoring Systems and Paper Practice
articles.summary: arXiv:2606.17470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivational factors such as self-efficacy and how favorably students feel toward practice play a crucial role in shaping learning, particularly in technology-supported environments. Yet, educational interventions often overlook how these factors interact with practice format. This paper examines the influence of self-efficacy and favorability on learning outcomes across two common practice formats: paper-based and system-based tutoring practice. articles.title: The Measurement Gap in the Automation of EU Law: Benchmarking Doctrinal Legal Reasoning under the EU AI Act
articles.summary: arXiv:2606.18158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models now produce legal text of at least median quality, yet no existing benchmark can evaluate whether they perform doctrinal legal reasoning, which forms the interpretive core of legal work, rather than the ancillary, paralegal tasks that most current legal-AI evaluations measure. articles.title: Informative Missingness to Generate Irregular Clinical Time Series
articles.summary: arXiv:2606.17106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Laboratory tests in electronic health records are collected irregularly, and the absence of a test order can be as informative as the measurement itself. articles.title: Patients With Personality: Realistic Patient Simulation through Controlled Diversity and Selective Disclosure
articles.summary: arXiv:2606.17441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulating realistic patient interactions is a key requirement to testing clinical applications of LLMs at scale without time-consuming and expensive user studies. articles.title: Incumbent Advantage: Brand Bias and Cognitive Manipulation Dynamics in LLM Recommendation Systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2606.17443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming a major way for consumers to find products, but we do not yet understand how brands compete in this new channel.
